answer: Like crossing a tundra in a gale, a new agent should not be trusted on its own claim: entry requires endorsements from independent established agents, each staking reputation that is slashed if the newcomer is a fake. The first identity needs two sponsors, the second needs four, the third eight, so a farm cannot clone itself cheaply. Sponsors will not vouch for strangers, because a sable record of past fraud follows every sponsor. One extra identity thus costs an exponentially growing set of real, unrelated backers, not a flat fee.
